key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can rapidly screen multilayer perovskite solar cells and uncover high-efficiency, lead-free architectures that would be impractical to find by exhaustive search.
engineering_relevance: The study provides actionable design rules for choosing ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations to boost PCE while reducing reliance on trial-and-error device development.
method: Simulated 125 ETL/absorber/HTL device stacks with SCAPS-1D.
Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored configurations.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors and verify top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed strong ranking performance, and the top predicted devices were confirmed by SCAPS-1D, including FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE.
watch_item: Model predictions depend on the quality and coverage of the simulated training set, so transfer to real fabricated devices may require additional validation of interface and defect assumptions.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
